title: Version bits with timeout and delay
summary: Mechanism for deploying soft forks in parallel through block-header version bits, with a start time, timeout and signalling threshold evaluated per 2016-block retarget period.
relevance: Drives the soft-fork section of the node dashboard (getdeploymentinfo, getblocktemplate rules/vbavailable/vbrequired) and the unknown-deployment warnings Bitcoin Core raises. Bitcoin Knots implemented BIP110 as a modified BIP9 deployment on bit 4, so BTCortex must show which deployments a node actually enforces.
implementedIn: bitcoin-knots (modified BIP9 temporary deployment for BIP110 from 29.3.knots20260508)

title: getblocktemplate - Fundamentals
summary: Defines the getblocktemplate JSON-RPC protocol through which mining software obtains a block template (transactions, coinbase value, target, rules) from a full node and submits solved blocks.
relevance: Mining and block-template views of the RPC workbench and any pool or solo-mining integration that talks to a managed node. Since 29.0 the curtime and mintime fields account for the BIP94 timewarp rule on all networks, so clients must use them rather than the local clock.

title: getblocktemplate - Pooled Mining
summary: Extensions to getblocktemplate for pooled mining, including long polling, block proposals and mutable template fields.
relevance: Long-polling and block-proposal behaviour used by mining tools connected to a managed node; relevant to BTCortex mining diagnostics.

title: Connection Bloom filtering
summary: P2P messages (filterload, filteradd, filterclear, merkleblock) that let light clients ask full nodes for transactions matching a Bloom filter.
relevance: Exposed as the -peerbloomfilters option (default 0 since 0.19.0) and the bloomfilter whitelist permission. The configuration editor should flag enabling it as a privacy and denial-of-service trade-off.

title: Consensus Cleanup
summary: Proposed soft fork fixing the timewarp vulnerability, worst-case block validation time (legacy signature-operation limits), 64-byte transactions and duplicate coinbase transactions.
relevance: Not active on mainnet. Bitcoin Core 29.1/30.0 made transactions with more than 2500 potentially executed legacy signature operations non-standard to prepare for a possible deployment, and Knots exposes the same limit as -maxtxlegacysigops; policy explanations and soft-fork monitoring in BTCortex should reference it.
implementedIn: bitcoin-core >= 29.1 (policy limit of 2500 legacy sigops only; no consensus deployment)

title: Testnet 4
summary: Specifies testnet4, a replacement for testnet3 with a new genesis block, a fixed 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception and a timewarp-attack mitigation.
relevance: Testnet4 environment manager and network profiles: -testnet4 or -chain=testnet4, configuration section [testnet4], data subdirectory testnet4, P2P port 48333 and RPC port 48332. Testnet3 is deprecated since 28.0 but still supported in 31.1.
implementedIn: bitcoin-knots (testnet4 hard-forked to BLAKE2b proof of work at height 150308 from 29.4.1.knots20260508)

title: Reduced Data Temporary Softfork
summary: Proposed one-year consensus restrictions on data-carrying constructs: scriptPubKeys over 34 bytes (OP_RETURN allowed up to 83 bytes), pushes and script-argument witness items over 256 bytes, spending undefined witness versions, Taproot annexes, control blocks over 257 bytes, OP_SUCCESS opcodes and OP_IF/OP_NOTIF in Tapscript, with pre-activation UTXOs exempt. Deployed on version bit 4 with a 55% threshold and mandatory signalling.
relevance: Explains the 2026 split between Bitcoin Knots and Bitcoin Core. Enforcing nodes rejected non-signalling blocks from height 961632 (2026-08-08); Knots 29.4.1.knots20260508 and later activate the rules together with a BLAKE2b proof-of-work hard fork at height 961640. BTCortex must detect which rules a node enforces, label the chain it follows and warn before connecting other services. Bitcoin Core does not implement it.
implementedIn: bitcoin-knots >= 29.3.knots20260508 (explicit consent required up to 29.4.knots20260508; unconditional from 29.4.1.knots20260508)

title: NODE_BLOOM service bit
summary: Service bit that signals support for BIP37 Bloom filtering, so nodes that disable it can be identified and peers that use filters without it can be disconnected.
relevance: Peer service flags shown in the peer monitor (servicesnames) and tied to the -peerbloomfilters option.

title: Opt-in Full Replace-by-Fee Signaling
summary: Defines nSequence-based signalling that a transaction may be replaced and the conditions a replacement must meet.
relevance: Mempool replacement analysis and wallet fee bumping. Bitcoin Core treats all transactions as replaceable since 28.0 (full RBF default) and removed -mempoolfullrbf in 29.0; 31.0 replaced the BIP125 rules with feerate-diagram checks (cluster mempool); 32.0 hides the bip125-replaceable fields unless -deprecatedrpc=bip125 and deprecates -walletrbf. Knots keeps -mempoolreplacement (default fee,-optin) and -mempoolfullrbf.

title: Segregated Witness (Consensus layer)
summary: Moves signature data into a separate witness structure, introduces block weight (4 000 000 weight units maximum) and virtual size, and defines witness programs.
relevance: Weight and virtual-size accounting in the explorer, mempool and fee tools, and the -blockmaxweight/-blockreservedweight options. 32.0 reports vsize_bip141 (raw BIP141 size) alongside vsize_adjusted (sigop-adjusted policy size).

title: Compact Block Relay
summary: Relays new blocks as short transaction IDs so peers can reconstruct them from their mempools, with high-bandwidth and low-bandwidth modes.
relevance: Block-propagation diagnostics in the peer monitor (getpeerinfo bip152_hb_to and bip152_hb_from) and the -blockreconstructionextratxn option; poor mempool coverage (for example -blocksonly) degrades reconstruction.

title: addrv2 message
summary: Address-relay message supporting variable-length network addresses such as Tor v3, I2P and CJDNS.
relevance: Needed for onion, I2P and CJDNS peers; the peer monitor and getnodeaddresses network filters (ipv4, ipv6, onion, i2p, cjdns) depend on it.

title: Client Side Block Filtering
summary: P2P protocol (getcfilters, getcfheaders, getcfcheckpt) through which light clients download compact block filters from full nodes, signalled by the NODE_COMPACT_FILTERS service bit.
relevance: Configuration option -peerblockfilters (requires -blockfilterindex=basic) to serve light clients such as Neutrino-based wallets from a managed node; exposure should be an explicit choice.

title: Compact Block Filters for Light Clients
summary: Defines the basic block filter (Golomb-coded set of scriptPubKeys spent and created in a block) and filter headers.
relevance: -blockfilterindex=basic enables getblockfilter, the REST blockfilter endpoints and fast wallet rescans via scanblocks; the index is compatible with pruning (it holds prune locks until indexed). Sparrow recommends it for faster rescans with Bitcoin Core 25 or later.

title: NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED service bit
summary: Service bit for pruned nodes that can serve at least the last 288 blocks.
relevance: Pruned node profiles (the default for constrained Windows machines) advertise NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED instead of NODE_NETWORK; peers and the peer monitor should reflect that such nodes cannot serve historical blocks.

title: 24 nVersion bits for general purpose use
summary: Reserves 24 block-header version bits for general-purpose use (for example by mining hardware) rather than soft-fork signalling.
relevance: From 32.0 (per the release-notes draft) Bitcoin Core ignores bits 5 to 28 for soft-fork signalling and no longer warns about unknown deployments when they are set, which changes the warnings BTCortex surfaces.
implementedIn: bitcoin-core >= 32.0 (per the release-notes draft; not yet released on 2026-10-21)

title: Version 2 P2P Encrypted Transport Protocol
summary: Opportunistically encrypted, pseudorandom-looking P2P transport using ElligatorSwift key exchange, with session IDs for optional authentication and the NODE_P2P_V2 service bit; replaces BIP151.
relevance: Peer monitor shows transport_protocol_type and session_id from getpeerinfo; -v2transport (default 1 since 27.0). The 31.0 private-broadcast IP leak was triggered by the v2-to-v1 fallback, so the transport matters for privacy diagnostics.

sources.title: Private Broadcast May Reveal Sender IP Address in Bitcoin Core 31.0

title: Signet
summary: Test network where blocks must additionally satisfy a signature challenge script, giving a predictable, centrally signed chain; custom signets use a different challenge.
relevance: Signet environment manager and custom signets (-signet, -signetchallenge, -signetseednode; getblockchaininfo returns signet_challenge). All signets use the signet/ data subdirectory, so each custom signet needs its own data directory. Ports 38333 and 38332.

title: Transaction announcements reconciliation
summary: Erlay: set reconciliation of transaction announcements between peers to reduce relay bandwidth.
relevance: Present in Bitcoin Core only as the debug-only -txreconciliation option (default 0); the configuration editor should mark it experimental and hidden.
implementedIn: bitcoin-core (partial, debug-only -txreconciliation, off by default in 31.1)

title: Ancestor Package Relay
summary: P2P messages for relaying a transaction together with its unconfirmed ancestors as a package.
relevance: Not implemented as P2P messages in Bitcoin Core; Core instead performs opportunistic one-parent-one-child (1p1c) package relay over the existing protocol (28.0+, extended in 30.0 and 31.0) and accepts packages through the submitpackage RPC. BTCortex's package-relay explanations must not claim BIP331 support.

title: WTXID-based transaction relay
summary: Announces and requests transactions by witness transaction ID to avoid repeatedly downloading malleated witnesses.
relevance: Transaction-relay diagnostics and mempool inspection; wtxid appears in mempool RPC output and ZMQ consumers must not confuse txid and wtxid.

title: Schnorr Signatures for secp256k1
summary: Schnorr signature scheme over secp256k1 with 32-byte x-only public keys and 64-byte signatures.
relevance: Script analysis, transaction decoding and Taproot tooling in the developer toolkit; MuSig2 (BIP327) support in Core 30.0/31.0 builds on it.

title: Taproot: SegWit version 1 spending rules
summary: SegWit version 1 outputs (P2TR) with key-path and script-path spending through a Merkle tree of scripts, new signature hashing and the annex.
relevance: Transaction decoder, descriptor and script tools; getdeploymentinfo no longer lists taproot in 32.0 (use script_flags). On Knots' chain BIP110 temporarily invalidates the annex and control blocks over 257 bytes for new outputs.

title: Validation of Taproot Scripts
summary: Tapscript: script semantics for Taproot leaves, including OP_CHECKSIGADD, OP_SUCCESS upgrade opcodes and revised resource limits.
relevance: Script analysis and Miniscript tooling; Knots' BIP110 rules restrict OP_SUCCESS and OP_IF/OP_NOTIF in new Tapscript spends on its chain, which wallet tooling must account for when targeting a Knots node.

title: Topology Restrictions for Pinning
summary: Topologically Restricted Until Confirmation (TRUC) policy for nVersion=3 transactions: at most one unconfirmed parent and one child, a 10 000 vB size limit, sibling eviction and zero-fee parents in packages.
relevance: Mempool policy explanations, package and CPFP analysis, and Lightning anchor-channel compatibility. Core relays TRUC since 28.0 and its wallet can create and spend TRUC transactions since 30.0 (version parameter on createrawtransaction, createpsbt, send, sendall, walletcreatefundedpsbt). Knots' -mempooltruc defaults to 'accept', i.e. it does not enforce TRUC limits by default.

title: Pay to Anchor (P2A)
summary: Standard keyless anchor output (witness v1, 2-byte program 0x4e73) that anyone can spend with an empty witness, used for fee bumping by child-pays-for-parent.
relevance: Ephemeral-anchor and CPFP analysis in the mempool tools. Spending P2A is standard in Core since 28.0 and ephemeral dust (one dust output in a zero-fee transaction that must be spent in the same package) since 29.0. Knots controls it with -permitbareanchor and -permitephemeral.

title: JSON-RPC 2.0 Specification
summary: Stateless, transport-agnostic remote procedure call protocol encoded in JSON: request and response objects, error objects with reserved codes (-32700 to -32600 range), notifications without id and batch arrays.
relevance: Bitcoin Core 28.0+ answers strictly per JSON-RPC 2.0 when a request carries "jsonrpc": "2.0" (HTTP 200 for RPC errors, HTTP 204 for notifications) and keeps legacy 1.1 behaviour otherwise (HTTP 400/404/500 on errors). BTCortex's RPC client should always send 2.0 requests and must handle Core's documented deviation of returning an empty array for an empty batch.

title: OpenRPC Specification
summary: Language-agnostic interface description for JSON-RPC 2.0 APIs, including method, parameter and result schemas and the rpc.discover service-discovery method.
relevance: Bitcoin Core 32.0 (release-notes draft) adds getopenrpcinfo and rpc.discover returning an OpenRPC 1.4.1 document of the node's RPCs; BTCortex can build its version-aware RPC catalogue and typed forms from it, falling back to parsing help output for older versions.
implementedIn: bitcoin-core >= 32.0 (per the release-notes draft; not yet released on 2026-10-21)
